guides.title: Flood
guides.summary: Before, during and after a flood

before: Move important documents, medicines and phone chargers to a waterproof bag now, before water rises.
Know your building's highest safe floor and the fastest route to higher ground.
Keep your emergency kit packed and easy to grab.
Charge phones and power banks when heavy rain or a flood warning is forecast.
during: If water is rising, move to higher ground immediately. Do not wait for it to enter your home.
Switch off electricity at the main switch if you can do so safely and the area is dry.
Stay away from rivers, drains and low-lying areas.
Use SETU SOS if there is no mobile network.
after: Do not return home until authorities say it is safe. Check for structural damage before entering.
Boil or treat drinking water until you know the local supply is safe again.
Photograph damage before cleaning up, then report it in SETU Recovery.
Wear boots and gloves when cleaning. Flood water can be contaminated.
avoid: Never walk or drive through moving flood water. 15 cm of fast water can knock an adult down.
Do not touch electrical equipment while standing in water.
Do not eat food that touched flood water.

guides.title: Earthquake
guides.summary: Before, during and after an earthquake

before: Identify solid furniture near you, such as a sturdy table or an interior wall corner, to shelter under or against.
Secure heavy furniture and shelves that could fall.
Agree on a family meeting point outside your building.
Keep shoes, a torch and a whistle within reach of your bed.
during: Drop, Cover, Hold On. Get under sturdy furniture and hold on until shaking stops.
Stay away from windows, mirrors and anything that could shatter.
If outdoors, move to an open area away from buildings, trees and power lines.
If in a vehicle, stop in a clear area and stay inside until shaking stops.
after: Expect aftershocks. Check yourself and others for injuries before moving around.
Exit the building calmly if it is damaged, using stairs.
If you smell gas, open windows and leave. Do not use flames or switches.
Listen for official updates and use SETU SOS if you are trapped or hurt.
avoid: Do not run outside during shaking; falling debris is the main danger.

guides.title: Cyclone
guides.summary: Before, during and after a cyclone

before: Follow official cyclone warnings and evacuation instructions for your area.
Pack an emergency kit with water, food, medicines, documents, a torch and a power bank.
Secure or bring in loose objects; shutter or tape windows if advised.
Know the location of your nearest cyclone shelter and how to reach it.
during: Stay indoors in a strong room, away from windows and glass doors.
Keep your phone charged and conserve battery.
If told to evacuate, go immediately to the designated shelter.
Stay inside even if the wind drops suddenly; the eye of the storm can pass before the wind returns.
after: Stay in shelter until authorities confirm it is safe.
Keep away from fallen power lines, damaged buildings and flooded roads.
Use only boiled or treated water until supply is confirmed safe.
Photograph damage and report it in SETU Recovery.
avoid: Do not go outside to watch the storm.
Do not shelter under trees or near loose structures.
Do not use candles or open flames near gas leaks.

guides.title: Fire
guides.summary: Before, during and after a fire emergency

before: Know two exit routes from your home or building, not just one.
Keep a fire extinguisher and a torch somewhere you can reach in the dark.
Do not block exits, stairwells or corridors.
Agree on a meeting point outside the building.
during: If you smell smoke, stay low. Cleaner air is near the floor.
Check doors for heat before opening them. If a door is hot, use your second exit.
Once outside, stay outside and call for help.
Use SETU SOS if the mobile network is down.
after: Do not re-enter until the fire service says it is safe.
Get medical attention for burns and smoke inhalation.
Do not touch damaged wiring or appliances.
Photograph damage and report it in SETU Recovery.
avoid: Never use a lift during a fire; use the stairs.
Do not go back in for belongings.
Do not throw water on an oil or electrical fire.

guides.title: Landslide
guides.summary: Before, during and after a landslide

before: Learn whether your area is prone to landslides and follow local warnings.
Watch for warning signs: new cracks in the ground, tilting trees or poles, muddy or unusual spring water.
Know an evacuation route that moves away from slopes and drainage channels.
Keep your emergency kit ready during heavy or prolonged rain.
during: If you notice rumbling or a sudden change in stream flow, move away from the path immediately.
Move to higher, stable ground, sideways out of the slide path rather than downhill.
If escape is not possible, curl into a tight ball and protect your head.
Use SETU SOS if you are trapped or injured.
after: Stay away from the slide area; more slides can follow.
Check for injured or trapped people and tell responders, but do not enter the slide area yourself.
Report broken utilities and blocked roads.
Have the slope and buildings checked by authorities before returning.
avoid: Do not cross or stay near a slide path.
Do not return to a damaged building until it is declared safe.
Do not travel on hill roads during heavy rain.

guides.title: Accident / General Emergency
guides.summary: What to do at the scene of an accident
steps: Check for danger to yourself before approaching — oncoming traffic, fire, unstable structures.
Call for help immediately. Use SETU's SOS if you have no signal.
Do not move an injured person unless they are in immediate danger (fire, traffic, flood).
If someone is bleeding heavily, apply firm, steady pressure with a clean cloth.
Keep the person calm and still until help arrives.
Note the location clearly — a nearby landmark helps responders find you faster.

guides.title: Women's Safety
guides.summary: Staying safe and reaching help quickly
steps: Share your live location with a trusted contact when travelling alone, especially at night.
Keep SETU's SOS quick-access enabled — a hold or volume-button trigger can call for help silently.
Trust your instincts. If a situation feels wrong, move to a public, well-lit place.
Memorise or save at least two emergency contacts who can act quickly.
If you are being followed, head toward the nearest open shop, guard post or crowd, not home.

guides.title: Child Safety
guides.summary: Preparing children and reporting a missing child
steps: Teach children their full name, a parent's phone number, and how to find a trusted adult (police, guard, shopkeeper) if lost.
Add your child's profile in SETU's Child Safety section so it's ready if needed.
Agree on a family meeting point in case you get separated during an emergency.
If a child goes missing, report it immediately — do not wait. Use SETU's lost child broadcast to alert nearby devices.
Give a clear, recent description: height, clothing, and where they were last seen.

guides.title: Senior Citizen Emergency
steps: Keep a list of current medications, dosages and doctor contact details somewhere accessible.
Save emergency contacts in SETU with clear labels (e.g. "Son — Ravi").
If a senior lives alone, agree on a daily check-in method with family.
Know the route to the nearest hospital and keep it saved offline.
During a disaster, mobility may be limited — plan an evacuation route that does not rely on stairs where possible.
